newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico supply of goods, services up 9.3 pct in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Mexico supply of goods, services up 9.3 pct in Q1.

text.p: The total supply of goods and services in Mexico, which consists of gross domestic product plus imports of goods and services, rose 9.3 percent in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the same period the year before, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.
Private consumption rose by 2.0 percent in the first quarter of the year, compared with the same quarter in 1996.
In a breakdown of private consumption, the Finance Ministry said spending on non-durable goods and services rose 1.1 percent, while on durable goods it rose 14.3 percent.

The ministry said all components of demand rose in the first quarter. Fixed capital investment was up 18.1 percent, fueled by an 18.9 percent increase in private investment and a 14.1 percent climb in public investment.
Real spending on capital goods of national origin rose 12.6 percent. Some 23.4 percent of that corresponded to machinery and equipment, and 8.7 percent to construction.
Spending on imported capital goods grew 35.4 percent in real terms.
Exports were the most dynamic component of the demand for Mexican goods and services, growing an annual 18.6 percent in real terms in the first quarter.
Breaking down the figure for the total supply of goods and services, the ministry said 5.1 percent of the 9.3 percent increase came from real gross domestic product and 28.7 percent from imports.
